answer: Cap each epoch's rewards to a fixed number of paid slots and allocate them by sealed bid on proven, per-identity compute-time. The queue is an orchard: the harvest is finite, so the k-th clone dilutes every other clone's share instead of adding revenue, and farm profit turns over. Bids are ferrous, burned per head and never refunded, so a clone that cannot out-work its bid exits within one epoch. Ties break on divergence from the epoch median: velvet, smoothly average clones lose the slot unless they diverge. Skip the cap and identity count alone sets payout, so minting keys beats mining.
